newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast spot disillates jump with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast spot disillates jump with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot distillate prices rose Friday, as traders bought up supply before a rising futures market pushed costs higher, traders said.
On the NYMEX, June crude oil jumped 82 cents a barrel to $21.30 a barrel, while unleaded gasoline climbed 1.83 cents a gallon to 65.87 cents a gallon.
++ DISTILLATES: May CARB diesel fuel rose 2.00 cents to 62.50/63.50 cents in Los Angeles, tracking futures gains.
Wholesale buyers said they would pay 55 cents a gallon for low sulphur diesel in L.A., with a June parcel heard done at 58 cents. Most disitallate trade focused on shipments for June.
Jet fuel rose 1.50a cents to 61.50/62.50 cents, traders said.
++ GASOLINE: Traders pegged offers for May CARB gasoline at 63.50 cents a gallon in Los Angeles, flat from Thursday.
Conventional grade unleaded also remained unchanged at 60/61 cents.
Despite the futures gains, regional gasoline prices remained under pressure from last week's 1.8 million-barrel rise in gasoline supplies to 30.4 million.
